scope: Six closely related works. Findings describe the papers; no research-gap claim is made.
review: Three agents each read two complete papers; final wording was cross-checked.

papers.read_version: Complete eight-page author manuscript; journal typesetting not separately audited.
findings: Output is a reconstructed trajectory and model complexity, not a per-window movement phase.
Supplied period supports cycle averaging; spherical angles predict radius after directional reduction.
Walking/running/electricity complexities are 3/6/8. Reconstruction error matters: running stops intersecting at dimension 4, yet complexity 6 is selected.
No phase ground truth or held-out phase validation is reported.

papers.read_version: Complete thirteen-page author manuscript marked DRAFT; Table II visually checked. Journal typesetting not separately audited.
papers.sections: Algorithm §§IV–V; moving windows §VI.B; results Table II, p.10; limitations p.11.
findings: Selects one consecutive PCA pair, not necessarily leading components; retains one orientation of symmetry-axis crossings.
Moving blocks span about ten periods; presented processing is not instantaneous causal estimation.
Table II printed F1 values are internally inconsistent with precision/recall. Type-2 PC: F1=.9953 exceeds (P+R)/2=.9017; separate averaging cannot explain this.
The exact rank-two argument applies to a pure sinusoid; arbitrary bounded amplitude can generate multiple sideband pairs. The Appendix does not establish its broader claim.
Self-intersections create extra crossings. Spectral-peak thresholds, reflection-point pairing and overlap reconciliation are not fully specified.

papers.read_version: Complete fourteen-page journal paper; relevant formulas, figures and tables visually checked.
papers.sections: Methods §2; synthetic comparisons §3.6; ECG §4; human motion §5; limits §6.
findings: Centered windows and normalized headings feed a circular network trained without phase labels.
Synthetic error SD is .047–.049 radians. Baselines receive one PCA channel; the network receives two channels and headings.
ECG and upper-limb tests are qualitative; human split is ten training and two unseen participants.
Reported short support excludes preprocessing. The printed synthetic formulas may have a period typo; code was not audited.
Project77 labels reference [22] a dual autoencoder, but that is this progression-network paper; its actual dual-autoencoder reference is [13], from 2017.

papers.read_version: Complete fourteen-page journal paper, including references and biographies.
papers.metadata: IEEE TSP 62(8), 2066–2079, 15 April 2014; DOI 10.1109/TSP.2014.2306174. The 2018 date previously mentioned in our discussion was incorrect.
papers.sections: Phase optimization §§III–IV; bias correction §V; evaluation §VI; limitations §§VII–VIII.
findings: One-record period estimation and self-DTW produce correspondences; global monotone optimization estimates phase.
Bias correction assumes that within-cycle warp fluctuations average to zero across cycles.
The presented method is offline and uses a period-range prior.
Synthetic phase ground truth supports evaluation. Real vision examples illustrate registration without labeled phase-error scores.

papers.read_version: Complete methods, results and discussion; PDF tables checked separately.
findings: Tibial angular velocity supports template fitting of phase, time scale, amplitude and offset.
Table 2, p.15 measures trajectory forecasting; Table 3, p.16 measures event timing, not circular phase RMSE.
The 70/30 split is not explicitly subject-disjoint.
Online solver details are unclear: §4.1.3, p.9 describes least squares; §5.2, p.13 excludes iterative optimization. These are not necessarily contradictory.
A short-horizon ablation narrative is inconsistent with the table; avoid claiming uniform ablation improvement.

papers.read_version: Complete preprint, including methods, results and discussion.
papers.sections: Matching §2.2; online protocol §4.2; results and limitations §5.
findings: Matches four joint-angle histories to 28 speed-indexed circular templates.
PCA models population-derived speed deformations; calibration comprises three speeds, with three 30-second online calibration trials.
Offline phase RMSE improves from 1.78% to 1.61%. Single-participant online results do not establish corrected pairwise significance.
Online trials use constant speeds; matching runtime excludes the full IMU pipeline.
This PCA acts on shape deviations, not Hankel windows.
